tier1.name: Functional / Stress Hardening
reportedRegressionRequirements: Game Center selected event follows the active game video on direct tune, Next, and automatic advance
Background program refresh cannot replace or restart the active media key
Manual pause remains latched for at least 25 seconds under background refresh
Score-ribbon date browsing cannot autoplay Silver daily/weekly roundup media
Production startup contains no legacy NBA/demo seed programming
Post-first-frame playback buffering self-recovers by failing over within a bounded window instead of hanging or restarting the same clip
Launch-started YouTube media enters a tracked playback session immediately and cannot remain indefinitely in starting while iframe readiness never arrives
Every clean-window error capable of blocking certification is exported with timestamp, category/code, source, message, detail/data, and browser/runtime identity
A count-only clean-window error with no corresponding exported error record cannot independently fail Tier 1; the diagnostic mismatch remains visible as an advisory

Known transient browser media interruptions are advisory only when a later PASS playback step plus a final PLAYING/OK playback session prove automatic recovery and are labeled RECOVERED_ADVISORY in the exported certificate

Post-test exact-state restoration is advisory unless final application health is bad; cleanup health requires restored resource mode, playback ownership OK, one soundtrack audio element, a selected media item on a started board, and Game Center consistency for game-scoped media
Playback watchdog failures that prove bounded automatic failover to a different PLAYING media asset and healthy post-test state are RECOVERED_ADVISORY rather than Tier 1 blockers.

Poisoned media is blocked before native/YouTube player assignment; any already-loading matching resources are torn down locally without resetting the healthy playback engine, and certification requires zero orphaned blocked loads.
Recap tier availability is keyed to physical playback identity: the same YouTube ID/direct URL cannot be advertised as both Green Quick and Purple Extended.
Known physical duration outranks conflicting discovery-objective metadata when assigning Quick versus Extended recap tiers.

Recent NFL weekly recap playlists are dynamically discovered from the official NFL YouTube channel; missing expected preseason/regular-season week catalogs trigger a bounded refresh instead of waiting on the long-lived playlist cache.
Custom competition creation is Dev Mode only and persists server-side.
Active special events appear in both Special Events and the main selector row; completed special events remain only under Special Events.
Custom event Game Center uses the canonical /api/events/<competition>/<event>/game-center contract.
World Cup and LLWS templates require schedule review before activation.
Competition Builder editable controls isolate keyboard input from document-level playback shortcuts so typing spaces/arrows cannot control playback.
Competition creation is not reported successful until the shared server store is written and a fresh definition read-back verifies persistence.
Custom competitions are enrolled in the canonical history league registry, operator playlist crawler, and dedicated background media gap-search worker.
Schedule Auto Discover uses structured output and falls back to direct extraction of an operator-supplied official schedule URL when web search fails.

Competition Builder schedule discovery is completeness-driven: large tournaments are researched in bounded date windows, merged/deduplicated, and checked against an expected event count instead of relying on one giant model response.
Site-wide competition creation rejects zero-event schedules and rejects incomplete schedules when an expected event count is known unless a future explicit override is introduced.

Dev Mode can delete a custom competition site-wide, removing its persisted definition, history event relationships, operator playlist registrations, runtime registry entry, and history-league crawl enrollment.
World Cup and LLWS templates carry deterministic completeness targets of 104 and 38 competition games respectively.
Special Events is a permanent top-level selector control; custom special-event catalog refreshes populate that stable control instead of transiently injecting/removing the control itself.
Selecting a completed or upcoming special event while browsing outside its event date range navigates the score ribbon into the event range before rendering its games.
Custom competition score hydration subscribes to the canonical ScoreDateStore browse-date authority so special-event games render on historical event dates across normal ribbon refreshes.
Special Events dropdown content is rendered in a viewport-level portal so the horizontally scrolling league-filter container cannot clip its menu.
Custom competition date hydration rebuilds the verified-media lookup used by score-card playback after schedule/media enter ScoreDateStore.
Custom operator playlist registrations are durably saved before asynchronous playlist crawl begins; existing custom competitions re-enroll media sources on server startup.
Custom event-media responses force canonical competition/event identity from the event relationship and lazily repair matching unassigned custom source media.
Competition Builder persists an explicit participant artwork strategy; the FIFA World Cup defaults to country flags while future competitions can choose team logos, provided artwork, auto, or none.
Competition Builder startup cannot recursively resolve the Special Events portal; the stable Special Events menu is read from the application DOM and may then be portaled to the viewport.
Competition Builder startup exposes READY/ERROR boot state and surfaces a visible Special Events warning if initialization fails instead of silently removing all custom-competition UI.
The 4.6.4 custom competition runtime bridge, participant artwork strategy, canonical custom-media identity repair, and verified-media lookup rebuild remain required in 4.6.5.

tier2.name: Extended Soak
requirements: At least 90% of expected 15-second telemetry samples are captured across the full soak window
No telemetry gap exceeds 2.5 sample intervals
Playback currentTime advances while state is playing; sustained no-progress beyond 45 seconds fails
Native video play-request acknowledgment is bounded so a pending HTMLMediaElement.play() Promise cannot delay first-frame recovery
Sustained buffering beyond 45 seconds fails
Timed-out game-transition calls are evidence and must recover within 20 seconds; only unrecovered transition timeouts fail the soak
Media decode/provider failures must self-recover to another playable selection rather than strand unattended playback
No playback ownership invariant violation
No same-media currentTime restart or same-media reselection regression
Game Center remains tied to game-scoped active media
Workers remain healthy during periodic platform snapshots
No milestone clean-window errors
No excessive JavaScript heap growth when browser heap telemetry is available

tier3.name: Controlled Chaos / Recovery
requirements: Background rerank storm preserves active playback
Aborted concurrent request storm recovers
Expected invalid-route failure is isolated from playback
Standby-player disruption does not disturb active playback
Resource-mode turbulence restores the original mode
Repeated game transitions preserve Game Center ownership
Manual pause survives concurrent API pressure
Post-chaos clean recovery window is healthy
Game Center provider 429 opens a bounded scheduler circuit and cancels queued background amplification
Tier 3 chaos evidence remains exportable through the post-chaos recovery reset
Timing-only WARN evidence remains visible and advisory; only failed assertions or failed recovery gates block Tier 3 certification

baseline: v4.6.5 restores the complete v4.6.4 custom-competition runtime bridge by fixing Competition Builder startup recursion, while retaining World Cup country flags, custom score/media hydration, canonical event-media repair, and all inherited Foundation requirements.
